reference.citation: M.E. Moebius, B.E. Lauderdale, S.R. Nagel & H.M. Jaeger, Nature 414, 270 (2001), DOI 10.1038/35104697, Fig. 1
reference.measured: rising time T_rise vs density ratio rho/rho_m and size ratio D/d

hypotheses.H1_direction: a large intruder denser than the bed (rho/rho_m = 3.24) rises (Brazil-nut ascent) at Gamma = 5
hypotheses.H2_nonmonotonic: T_rise(rho/rho_m) is non-monotonic with an interior maximum near rho/rho_m ~ 0.5 (the reference's rho*/rho_m ~ 0.47-0.5, measured on the ambient-pressure branch)
hypotheses.H3_size: the rise time decreases as D/d grows (size dependence becomes pronounced for large D/d)

metrics.T_rise: taps from release until the intruder top reaches the free surface (censored at the tap budget)
metrics.rise_per_tap: mean increase of intruder centre height per tap, in units of the small-particle diameter d

tolerances.qualitative: sign/direction and the ordering of T_rise must match the reference trend
tolerances.quantitative: T_rise relative error < 20 % for trend descriptors that the reference reports numerically
tolerances.withheld: absolute T_rise values of the reference are only published graphically (Fig. 1, paywalled body); they are marked WITHHELD, never digitised by guesswork

scale_gap.D_over_d: 8 (reference 50.8): a 1:1 reproduction needs ~1e4 particles across the bed depth; declared, not hidden
scale_gap.air: the 2D dry-disk engine has no interstitial gas; the reference's pressure branch (90 torr) is out of scope for this round
